verdictRationale: The workspace family that exists is a BROKERAGE (real-estate-agent) property-workspace feature, not a city file system. It is real and serving on the reporting gate, but it is a different product for a different buyer, and the three load-bearing Smart Files promises (one search across everything a city holds; a document lives once and appears everywhere it belongs; revise once, current everywhere, prior version still there) are each structurally impossible in the schema that exists. There is no city-file substrate to render. Doc 34 open-item 1 is FALSIFIED.
verdictNotRenderingPassBecause: Scope mismatch: every artifact is self-labelled 'Brokerage V1' / domain 'brokerage'. Contract package description: 'Brokerage workspace packaging contract types for V1.' Engine package description: 'Brokerage V1 property-workspace atom emission, indexing, and retrieval.' No city, department, records-retention, or municipal-document concept exists anywhere in the family.

'A document lives once and appears everywhere it belongs' is structurally impossible: brokerage_workspace_attachments.workspace_id is a single NOT NULL uuid FK with onDelete cascade. One attachment row belongs to exactly ONE workspace. There is no many-to-many join table. Many placements = many copies, the exact problem Smart Files claims to solve.

'Revise once, current everywhere - and what it was before is still there' has no code path: brokerage_workspace_attachments has NO updated_at column and NO version column, and grep for update(brokerageWorkspaceAttachments across artifacts/api-server/src returns zero hits. The only mutations are insert and delete. Attachments cannot be revised at all, so neither propagation nor history exists for documents.

'One search across everything the city holds' has no search path: no full-text index, no tsvector column, no search route over attachments. Retrieval is by workspace id or by owner/install listing only.
The atom-store leg is absent: zero workspace-family atoms exist in the 67.5M-row hauska_mcp.atoms table, and no SQL migration creating a workspace atom table exists in hauska-engine.

laneAShouldBuild.why: Every existing artifact is brokerage: a workspace is keyed by (installId, listingKey) - a real-estate listing opened by an agent's browser extension. A city Smart File needs department, record series, retention schedule, and a records-officer owner. None of these concepts exist in any layer.
laneAShouldBuild.size: new contract family, not a rename

laneAShouldBuild.why: The approved claim 'a document lives once and appears everywhere it belongs' requires a join table. brokerage_workspace_attachments.workspace_id is a single NOT NULL FK with cascade delete. This is the single largest gap between the claim and the code.

laneAShouldBuild.item: Document revision with retained prior versions
laneAShouldBuild.why: The approved claim 'revise once and it is updated everywhere - and what it was before is still there' has NO implementation: no updated_at, no version column, no update route, and zero .updated events ever emitted despite the event type being declared in the engine registry.
'One search across everything your city holds' has no index and no route. Retrieval today is by workspace id or owner listing only.

@hauska-engine/workspace's only WorkspaceStoragePort implementation is an in-memory Map, the package has zero consumers, no SQL migration exists, and there are zero workspace atoms in the 67.58M-row atom store. The atom leg of the family is entirely unbuilt.

Doc 34 line 44 claims 'access is a property of the record, resolved at read time (ADR-017)'. The serving tables carry NO access_policy column; access is resolved by installId/ownerUserId ownership checks. The lens model the doc promises does not exist on this data.

Zero surfaces render workspace atoms. command-center (contradicting doc 34 line 32), property-explorer, and smartcity-os all return zero hits. This part IS a rendering build, but it has nothing to render onto yet.

Doc 34 lines 66 and 129 assert 'atoms and nodes are already programmed with CID identifiers' and rest the portability claim on it. NOT VERIFIED in this audit: no cid or content-address field appears in the workspace contract metadata schema (did/createdAt/updatedAt/accessPolicy only) or in the serving tables. The engine emit.ts computes a sha256 contentHash, which is a hash, not a CID. Treat the CID claim as unsubstantiated for this family.
laneAShouldBuild.size: unknown; verify before any collateral relies on it

openQuestions: Is there a SEPARATE city-file substrate somewhere this audit did not reach? This audit searched hauska-atom-contract, hauska-engine, hauska-mcp-server, legacy-design-tools, hauska-map (PE + command-center), and smartcity-os. All local clones. A repo not on P:/ was not searched.
